livia03.title: The Pilgrim
livia03.d01: Dusk. Guarding the gate is the most tedious task in the Temple, and so the most dangerous: it is through boredom that things get in.
livia03.d01a: If you need me, I'm here. I still hear the knocking at night. You hear it too, don't you?
livia03.d01b: Cláudia is at the back of the Temple, her back turned. Since the morning of the flame, she hasn't spoken to Lívia.
livia03.d02: Someone knocks at the gate. Not like someone asking. Like someone who has knocked on many doors.
livia03.h.lamp.1: In the lamp, the flame still leans toward the floor. No one else seems to notice. Or everyone pretends.
livia03.h.amphora.1: Domícia had the amphora filled twice this week. The flame has been drinking more. Like a sick man with a fever.
livia03.d03: Priestess. They told me that here the flame never goes out.
livia03.d04: They told you right. What do you seek in the Temple of Vesta?
livia03.d05: My name is Iante. I come from the port, and before the port, from Corinth. My son, Díon, has had a fever for nine days.
livia03.d06: The healer said he would die on the third. I wept on the third. He didn't die.
livia03.d08: Generous? At night he gets up, walks to the window and says the same words. Every night. The same.
livia03.d11: I want an ember from your flame. Just one. So that he can go.
livia03.c01: Iante doesn't blink. Mothers who have already wept everything don't blink.
livia03.c01.law: "The flame of Vesta never leaves this Temple."
livia03.d12: Where everyone goes. Where he should already have gone. He's tired, priestess. I see it in his eyes.
livia03.g03.hint: Iante isn't lying about her son. But what is she hiding under her cloak?
livia03.g03.key: The bronze key of a shrine of Hestia, the old name of Vesta in the provinces.
livia03.g03.coin: A coin sewn into the hem: the obol for the ferryman of the dead.
livia03.g03.all: Saw everything Iante was hiding: the key and the coin.
livia03.g03.some: Saw part of what Iante was hiding.
livia03.g03.none: Raised the flame before Iante and saw nothing.
livia03.d16: Of a name you say is the same. If it's the same, then the flame is mine too.
livia03.d16coin: And you've already paid the ferryman.
livia03.d16coin2: Mothers pay in advance, priestess. It's the only thing we can do in advance.
livia03.d17none: The flame shows nothing. Iante keeps looking at it, waiting.
livia03.d17: Something creaks inside Lívia, like an old beam. It doesn't break. Not yet.
livia03.d18: The Temple does not lend out Vesta, woman. Not even for mothers. Especially not for mothers.
livia03.d19: She says it harshly, but she doesn't look at Iante while she speaks. She looks at the floor.
livia03.c02: Iante looks at Lívia, not at Domícia.
livia03.c02.refuse: "I'm sorry. The flame cannot leave this place."
livia03.c02.promise: Promise, in a low voice, to bring an ember to the port after the Night Rite.
livia03.c02.bless: "Let me bless your son in the name of Vesta. He will find peace."
livia03.d20a: I'm sorry. The flame cannot leave this place.
livia03.d21a: Then he'll keep walking to the window. And I'll keep listening.
livia03.d20b: Lívia speaks low, barely moving her lips: after the Night Rite, at the port. Iante understands before she finishes.
livia03.d21b_ok: If Domícia heard, she says nothing. Perhaps that is exactly why she heard.
livia03.d20c: Let me bless your son in the name of Vesta. He will find peace.
livia03.d21c: Peace. Thank you, priestess. Perhaps that's all he needs.
livia03.d22: The sun sinks behind the hills. At the back of the Temple, under the altar, the knocking starts again. Stronger. Closer.
livia03.d22crack: A knock stronger than all the others. The floor by the altar cracks, and a new fissure, thin as a hair, runs across the stone to Lívia's feet.
livia03.d23a: You heard it now. Say you heard it.
livia03.d23b: It's nothing. It's the Temple settling. Old temples settle.
livia03.c03: The knocking stops as soon as she pays attention.
livia03.d24a: Lívia tells Domícia everything. Domícia listens without interrupting and, at the end, says only:
livia03.d24a2: Don't go down. Never go down.
livia03.d24b: Lívia keeps the knocking with the other things she doesn't say. The box is already full.
livia03.h.augur.1: The augur Varrão has come back to the Temple. He doesn't pray, doesn't ask. He counts the Vestals with his eyes, and he begins and ends the count with Domícia.
livia03.h.augur.2: Varrão is near the altar now, too near. When Lívia passes, he doesn't pretend not to look. On his tablet, a single word, underlined twice: "Chief".
livia03.d05b: As she speaks, her hand keeps going back to the hem of her cloak, like someone checking that a thing is still there.
livia03.gh: what is Iante hiding under her cloak?
livia03.t_c02: The law says no. The mother says please. Both are right.
livia03.t_c02.second: "Protect the Temple, girl, and the Temple protects you."
livia03.c02.claim: "She is a priestess of Hestia, Domícia. The flame is hers too."
livia03.d_claim: The key at her belt is from a shrine of Hestia. She is a priestess, Domícia. If the flame is the same, she isn't asking to borrow it. She is asking for it back.
livia03.d_claim2: ...Hestia. It's been thirty years since I heard that name said in earnest. Do what you must, Lívia. I heard nothing. And you will owe me for it.
livia03.d21b_ceded: Domícia looks at the floor, as she promised. She heard nothing. But she will remember not hearing it.
